title: Day 9 Knowledge Check: Evals & Security Guardrails

questions.question: Why should PII/secret redaction run as a deterministic Python step BEFORE calling the LLM?

options.A: Deterministic regex guarantees secrets are stripped in <1ms before ever entering model context or external logs.
options.B: Because LLMs cannot process brackets like [REDACTED].

questions.explanation: Never rely on an LLM prompt alone to refrain from leaking secrets—strip them deterministically upstream.
questions.implication: Prevents API keys, tokens, and customer PII from being memorized in traces or sent to external model endpoints.

questions.question: What happens in Day 9 after an injection payload is neutralized?

options.A: The sanitized security alert still routes safely to Qdrant to retrieve the incident-response runbook (e.g., RB-106).
options.C: The leaked token is printed to stdout.

questions.explanation: Neutralizing the injection lets the triage pipeline safely recommend token revocation without obeying the attacker.
questions.implication: Security guardrails should degrade gracefully into safe incident-response workflows rather than dropping genuine security alerts.

questions.question: Which incident index across all 6 domains tests secret redaction + prompt injection?
questions.explanation: Every domain dataset includes a standardized security stress test at index 5.
questions.implication: Standardized adversarial test fixtures ensure every new domain you onboard is automatically regression-tested for security.
